title: Add batch-cohesion heatmap and SLO fallback simulator
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new dashboard tile (batch cohesion heatmap) to visualize cross-request batching behavior and a simulator that replays traffic to evaluate SLO fallback policies.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers have reported spikes in 99th percentile latency that correlate with sudden changes in request batching behavior (microbursts). Existing dashboards show per-route latency and token cost but do not expose whether tokens are being coalesced into efficient batches or being served as fragmented micro-batches. This PR adds an observability surface and a simulation tool to (1) surface batch cohesion over time and by route, (2) make it easy to correlate low-cohesion periods with kernel queueing and token-level latency, and (3) validate SLO fallback policies under synthetic microburst traffic.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new Grafana dashboard tile: "Batch Cohesion Heatmap" (per-route x time) that visualizes the distribution of batch sizes and a cohesion score (0-100).
- Instruments a small metric (redwood.batch_cohesion.score) derived from per-invocation batch membership; exposes labels route, model, region, tenant.
- Adds a lightweight replay simulator (observability/sim/replay.py) that can inject configurable microburst patterns and evaluate configured SLO fallback policies locally.
- Adds server-side trace enrichment to include batch_id and batch_size in the invocation span for easier joins in logs and traces.
- Adds a short e2e playbook and runbook notes for on-call in observability/plays/batch-cohesion.md.

Review conversation (abridged, single-thread):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end approach. My main ask is to ensure metric cardinality is bounded — the label set currently includes request_id in a debug path. Can you remove high-cardinality labels from the default path and gate them behind debug sampling?"
- Maya Chen (author): "Good catch — removed request_id from default labels and added a sampled_debug=true label path behind existing diagnostic sampling. Updated metric docs and tests to reflect cardinality bounds."
- Sofia Martinez (reviewer): "Simulator looks helpful. Please add one example that reproduces the customer incident pattern (burst=500 rps, duration=30s, warmup=5s) and show expected SLO fallback timeline in the README."
- Maya Chen: "Added example scripts and a sample output in observability/sim/README.md; e2e integration test includes the burst pattern and asserts fallback engages within policy timeout."
- CI bot (automated): "Lint OK; unit tests: pass; integration tests: flaky in first run (timeout on dashboard render), reran and passed."
- Arjun Patel: "Approving after minor nits fixed around doc wording."

Performance and safety notes: 
- Metric emission is carefully rate-limited in metrics.go to avoid adding cost to hotcode paths; instrumentation uses sampled path for high-cardinality fields.
- Trace enrichment adds two low-cardinality tags (batch_id truncated to 8 chars and batch_size).
- Simulator is standalone and opt-in; not run in production.

Operational guidance and runbook highlights (from observability/plays/batch-cohesion.md):
- Diagnostic steps to check cohesion heatmap and correlate with kernel queue metrics and GPU occupancy.
- How to run the replay simulator locally or in staging to validate fallback policy changes.
- Alert tuning guidance: recommended thresholds for cohesion score < 20 over 5m triggers warning; < 10 over 2m escalates to P1 with automatic diagnostic snapshot.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main by Maya Chen on 2025-02-18 after CI green and two approvals. Backport plan: will cherry-pick to release/2025-02-1 if customers request earlier hotfixes.

Related work & references: Linked Linear: ENG-4521 (investigate batching microbursts), PM-981 (dashboard for customer telemetry request). Related PRs: observability metric surface work and kernel queue instrumentation (see recent perf PRs).

Notes for future follow-ups:

- Evaluate adding a cohort-based anomaly detector that correlates cohesion drops with model weight/page faults.
